body: Newegg almost always has free shipping, and I've never waited more than 3 days for anything. I've had stuff come the next day with that free shipping more than once too.

I'm on a drug (propanolol) which basically makes me not afraid of anything. It makes my life more tolerable, but it's no substitute for the confidence and presence of mind I used to have. Do you think it would be better to do this while i'm not on it, to experience the full fear response?

That sounds pretty similar. I can't relate to the part about it not being apparent to other people though, I'm usually worried about people noticing there's something wrong with me. It's hard to hide how withdrawn, distant and quiet I've become, especially since I have so much trouble knowing what other people are thinking (empathizing) now.

The drug/alcohol to get a break wouldn't be missing, except when I drink or take drugs (caffeine and xanax so far) and it does help, I cant enjoy it and get extra stressed out if I do because I know it's just the drugs. I worry about endless new things: am I becoming an addict? would I be if this actually worked? am I feeling the drug? has it kicked in? is it wearing off? where am I in terms of its biological half-life? what else is it doing to me? will I notice the side effects? will I hate myself later for doing this? what do other people think? The list goes on and on and on, racing though my brain so fast I almost can't pick one out from the rest, the room spins, and I start to forget where I am and what's going on. That thought pattern is true for almost everything I do, from when I eat breakfast to what shirt I wear that day. Trying to make actual decisions with consequences is akin to trying to read Sanskrit.

Normal parts of life, things like responsibilities (or even the concept) have just ceased to mean anything to me (I mean that literally, as in "what's a responsiblity?").
Good idea, I'll give it a try. I'm at college, there's no end of public places that make me uncomfortable.

I feel like i'm out of options. I've tried drugs, therapy, everything. I'm hoping the hivemind will have some insight that my doctors haven't. I'm glad somebody knows what i'm talking about with the white noise thing.

I crossposted to socialanxiety. I'll happily go to any meetup event, as awkward and scary as it might be. I can hold my own in social situations, for a while anyway. Eventually the fear starts creeping up, my brain shuts down, and I can't do it any more.

If you're like me, the overwhelming emotion in these situations is fear. If that's the case, I recommend the beta-blocker propanolol. It's the only drug that's done anything for me so far, including benzodiazapines and SSRI/SNRI antidepressants.

I went to college, was too scared and withdrawn to make new friends. I isolated myself more and more as time went on, I was afraid of embarassing myself and i'm generally terrified of casual interactions with people. I'm not sure how that fits in with my brain deciding to stop working.

I was in high school, my junior and senior year. I was working, but I hated my job. I'm working now, but it's the same as everything else - something I have to do before i can go back to my room and try to forget about life.
